# Home Assistant integration for UniFi Drive / UNAS v0.9.0

A reliability and quality update for local UNAS monitoring and control. Existing
`0.8.0+` installations update normally: no new domain change, reinstall or entity
migration is required.

## Changes

- Fixes reauthentication and reconfiguration on Home Assistant `2024.8.0`, with
  tests that reject a different device without changing existing credentials.
- Caps decompressed HTTP response bodies at 8 MiB across monitoring, login,
  errors and actions. Oversized responses fail with a privacy-safe error rather
  than accumulating an unrestricted response body.
- Adds actual HA flow-manager tests for setup retry/abort, options validation,
  identity preservation, reloads and repair recovery.
- Adds real SQLite Recorder tests for unchanged polling, throughput exclusions,
  cached offline data and snapshot-control attribute deduplication.
- Measures repeated setup/unload and continuous polling with changing snapshot
  targets. Inventory caches drop inactive targets; existing entity groups remain
  available for automations and missing-target handling.
- Expands strict typing to every integration module and checks selected HA
  interfaces against real imported types.
- Adds scheduled synthetic resource checks and verifies published release tags,
  notes and installation ZIPs against the release source.

## Compatibility And Scope

The tested HA baselines remain `2024.8.0` / Python `3.12` and `2026.10.4` /
Python `3.14`. HA `2026.11` is not required. Full November and Marketplace
lifecycle validation remain separate follow-up work.

The full local suite passes 762 tests on each baseline, with coverage above 95%.
Resource measurements are synthetic regression tests, not a new live NAS soak or
a guarantee of constant RAM with unlimited new snapshot target identities.
Global Recorder settings, statistics retention and purge behavior are unchanged.

Cached offline readings and Wake-on-LAN are preserved. Local snapshot, fan,
backup and update controls remain experimental and firmware/permission dependent.
No destructive snapshot actions are added. Quality Scale gaps remain documented;
this is not an official Platinum certification.

## Updating

For integration versions `0.8.0` and newer, back up Home Assistant, install the
offered update and complete any requested restart. Keep the existing integration
entry, device and entities. Moving from HACS to Marketplace does not require a
reinstall.

**Versions before `0.8.0` require removal and reinstallation** because the old
`unifi_drive` domain was replaced by `unifi_unas`. This is the earlier breaking
change, not a new migration introduced in `0.9.0`:

1. Back up Home Assistant and note affected automation/dashboard references.
2. Remove the old integration entries under `Settings` -> `Devices & services`.
3. Uninstall the downloaded integration through HACS or Marketplace to remove its
   managed files. Deleting only a device or config entry does not remove the code.
4. For manual installations, or if the old folder remains after uninstalling,
   remove only `/config/custom_components/unifi_drive/`. Do not edit `.storage`.
5. Restart Home Assistant, install the current integration through the appropriate
   installation method, then add **UniFi Drive / UNAS** again.
6. Check affected automations and dashboards. Do not retain both domains for the
   same NAS.

See the [installation guide](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-unifi-drive/blob/v0.9.0/docs/installation.md)
for Marketplace, HACS and manual procedures.
